title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: GAR Resp — hard to see how that proves Adam's-sin imputation; no confused hypostasis
pass_a_gloss: Garrigues answers that Placeus's reason hardly assigns Adam's-sin imputation. No champion of that view, he says, ever dreamed his person (or anyone's) fused with Adam into one hypostasis—such confusion is not even thinkable.
pass_b_english: GAR. Resp. It is hard enough to see and say how the force of this reason assigns the imputation of Adam's sin. For either I am far wrong, or none of those who fight for this imputation ever dreamed that his own person, or any other man's, is confused with Adam's person, or so indistinct as to have coalesced into one hypostasis with him. That cannot even be conceived in the mind. Etc.
source_text: GAR. Resp. Huius rationis vim satis ad assignandam peccati Adami imputationem videre difficile est & dicere. Nam aut longe fallor, aut nemo eorum qui pro hac imputatione pugnant, unquam somniavit personam suam, vel alterius cuiuscumque hominis, esse confusam cum persona Adami, aut ita indistinctam, ut in unum ὑπόστασιν cum ea coaluerit. Hoc ne quidem animo concipi potest. &c.

choices.choice: Doesn't prove imputation; no hypostatic fusion
